title: Blichfeldt's Theorem: k+1 Congruent Points When vol > k

problemStatement.formal: \text{If } S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n \text{ is measurable with } \mathrm{vol}(S) > k, \text{ then } S \text{ contains } k+1 \text{ points with pairwise differences in } \mathbb{Z}^n
problemStatement.plain: Blichfeldt's theorem (1914): any measurable set S in R^n with volume > k contains k+1 distinct points x_1,...,x_{k+1} whose pairwise differences all lie in the integer lattice Z^n. Unlike Minkowski's theorem, no convexity or symmetry is needed.

S10 (researcher-12, 2026-05-08): The Path A `tsum-of-indicators → encard` bridge is 2 lines (not 35): `rw [tsum_congr h_summand_eq, ← tsum_subtype, ENNReal.tsum_set_one]`. `tsum_subtype` (used by Mathlib's `Measure.Count.le_count_apply`) provides `∑' _ : ↥s, f _ = ∑' i, s.indicator f i`; combined with `ENNReal.tsum_set_one` (`∑' _ : ↥s, 1 = s.encard`) the covering-count function evaluates to `T(z).encard` where `T(z) := {v : L | (v : ℝⁿ) + z ∈ s}`. S10 (researcher-12, 2026-05-08): Path A contrapose unwrap is non-trivial: the goal `∃ pts : Fin (k+1) → ℝⁿ, ...` reformulates cleanly to `∃ z, ∃ vs : Fin (k+1) → L, Injective vs ∧ ∀ i, z + (vs i : ℝⁿ) ∈ s` (factoring out the lattice translation). pts := z + (vs i : ℝⁿ) recovers the original via add_left_cancel + AddSubgroupClass.coe_sub. After contrapose+push_neg, the hypothesis becomes `∀ z, ∀ vs (inj), ∃ i, z + vs i ∉ s`, equivalent to `∀ z, T(z).encard ≤ k` — directly bounded by `setLIntegral_mono_ae`.
